articles.title: Nottingham Forest stun Chelsea 3-2 in five-goal Premier League thriller
articles.summary: However, Forest struck again in the 72nd minute through Gibbs-White, who collected a pass inside the box and lifted the ball over Martínez to restore the hosts' two-goal cushion.
articles.hausa_translation: Nottingham Forest ta bugi Chelsea da ci 3-2 a wasan Premier League mai ban mamaki. Forest ta samu ƙarin gida a minttin 72 lokacin da Gibbs-White ya karɓi wasan a cikin akwati kuma ya lika ballen akan Martínez domin komawa ga gida.
critical_questions: What were the full match circumstances and tactical factors that allowed Forest to overturn any deficit?
How does this result affect both teams' league positions and their competitive trajectories this season?
Were there controversial refereeing decisions in this match that influenced the outcome?
What is the injury or suspension status of key players for both teams that may have impacted performance?
Is the source (PM News) covering this match with any geographic or editorial bias toward either club?

articles.title: NGX investors gain N534bn as equities rally, market value hits N159trn
articles.summary: Zenith Bank also recorded a strong performance, appreciating by 5.88 per cent to close at N108 per share from N102.
articles.hausa_translation: Masu jarin kudin NGX suka samun N534bn yayin da kasuwa ta tashi, kimar kasuwa ta isa N159trn. Zenith Bank kuma ya samu karfi sosai, yana tashi kashi 5.88 kolin kuma ya rufe a N108 bawon daga N102.
critical_questions: Who benefits most from this rally - retail investors or institutional/elite investors with large holdings?
What specific market catalysts or news drove this N534bn gain, and is this sustainable or speculative?
Why did Zenith Bank specifically outperform, and does this reflect genuine fundamentals or concentrated buying pressure?
How does this market value compare to economic fundamentals, GDP, and corporate earnings - is the market overvalued?
Are ordinary Nigerians actually participating in these gains, or is wealth concentration increasing among existing shareholders?

articles.title: Actress Mosunmola Adeleye rallies Yewa support for Yayi
articles.summary:
Nollywood actress, grassroots mobiliser and philanthropist, Mosunmola Adeleye, has thrown her weight behind the aspiration of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, calling on the people of Yewa to unite and rally support for his ambition to lead Ogun State.
The post Actress Mosunmola Adeleye rallies Yewa support for Yayi appeared first on Tribune Online.
articles.hausa_translation: Aktirisar Nollywood, Mosunmola Adeleye, ta bada godar Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, da aka sani da Yayi, a neman jagorancin jihar Ogun. Ta kira jama'ar Yewa su haɗa gida su bada godar niyarsa.
critical_questions: What specific political or financial incentives motivated Adeleye's endorsement at this particular timing in the electoral cycle?
Who is funding this grassroots mobilization effort, and does Adeleye's philanthropic work receive support from Yayi's political network?
Where are the opposing voices or candidates' supporters in Yewa region, and why does the article present only one perspective?
What evidence exists that this endorsement reflects genuine grassroots support versus celebrity influence marketing for a political candidate?
Does the source (Tribune Online) have documented ownership connections to any political parties or figures backing Yayi's ambition?

articles.title: Saint Anne’s School old girls urge increased govt investment in schools
articles.summary:
The old students of Saint Anne’s School Ibadan, under the umbrella of the Seminary-Saint Anne’s School Old Girls Association (SSASOGA), have demanded more resources and support from the Oyo State government for the development of the school and the students.
The post Saint Anne’s School old girls urge increased govt investment in schools appeared first on Tribune Online.
articles.hausa_translation: Tsofaffiyar almajiriya ta Saint Anne's School Ibadan, a ƙarƙar ƙungiyar Seminary-Saint Anne's School Old Girls Association (SSASOGA), sun bukaci karuwar albarkatun da goyon bayan gwamnatin Jihar Oyo don haɓakar makarantar da ɗalibi.
critical_questions: What specific funding gaps or infrastructure deficiencies prompted this demand, and what evidence supports these claims?
How much additional investment is SSASOGA requesting, and has the Oyo State government responded or committed to any timeline?
Why are only old girls making this appeal—are current students, parents, or staff not involved, and does this represent broader school concerns?
What is SSASOGA's track record of advocacy, and do they have political or business interests that could benefit from increased government investment?
How does Saint Anne's School funding compare to other private/mission schools in Ibadan, and is this complaint unique or part of a wider sector crisis?

articles.title: Engineers charge Ibadan students on tech innovation as winners emerge from engineering challenge
articles.summary:
The next generation of Nigerian engineers may already be sitting in secondary school classrooms, waiting for the right opportunity to turn their ideas into practical solutions. 
The post Engineers charge Ibadan students on tech innovation as winners emerge from engineering challenge appeared first on Tribune Online.
articles.hausa_translation: Injiniyoyi suna bugi dalibai Ibadan akan fasahar samarwa kamar masu nasara suka fito daga gaggawan injiniya
critical_questions: Who organized and funded this engineering challenge, and what are their vested interests in promoting tech innovation in Ibadan specifically?
What specific problems or solutions did winning students propose, and do they address actual market needs or investor priorities?
Whose voices are missing—were rural students, girls in STEM, or students from under-resourced schools adequately represented and able to participate?
What happens to these 'next generation engineers' after the challenge ends—is there documented follow-up support, funding, or mentorship?
Why frame secondary school students as 'waiting for the right opportunity' rather than examining systemic barriers in Nigerian engineering education and job markets?

articles.title: The past and Ademola Adeleke’s era in Osun
articles.summary:
Every state has a before and an after. In Osun State, the gap between past administrations and the administration of Governor Ademola Adeleke is not merely a change of government. It is, in the telling of his administration and its supporters, a change of philosophy...
The post The past and Ademola Adeleke’s era in Osun appeared first on Tribune Online.
articles.hausa_translation: Jiya da zamanin Ademola Adeleke a Osun: Kowane jiha yana da 'kafin da bayan'. A Osun State, bambanci tsakanin gwamnatin da ta gabata da gwamnatin Governar Ademola Adeleke ba kawai jiya baje ne ba. A cewar faɗin administarashi da marubuciyinsa, hanya ta falsafa ta canja.
critical_questions: What specific policies or achievements constitute the 'change of philosophy' claimed, and where is the empirical evidence?
Who benefits from this narrative of stark contrast between past and present, and does it oversimplify governance complexities?
What perspectives from opposition parties or previous administrations are absent from this framing?
Is 'his administration and its supporters' the primary source, and what independent verification exists for these claims?
What measurable outcomes (economic, social, infrastructural) support this 'change of era' beyond rhetorical positioning?

articles.title: Ransomware Attacks Could Cost African Firms $368,000 Per Incident
articles.summary: African businesses could lose an estimated $368,319 from a single ransomware incident that disrupts operations, as rising cyber threats expose companies to financial losses, operational disruptions and reputational damage. A new study by cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, in collaboration with research consultancy VDC Strategy, estimated that the global average financial impact of a disruptive ransomwa
articles.hausa_translation: Zartawar Ransomware Na Iya Kashe Kudin Kamfanoni na Afrika $368,000 A Kowane Abin Da Ya Faru
critical_questions: Who commissioned this Kaspersky-VDC Strategy study and what commercial interest might they have in inflating these damage estimates to drive security software sales?
What percentage of African businesses actually experienced ransomware attacks versus projections, and are these figures extrapolated from limited sample sizes?
Why does the article lack specific case studies or verified incidents from African firms, instead relying on global averages that may not reflect regional capacity and actual losses?
Are African businesses actually paying these ransom amounts, or is this theoretical financial impact inflated by insurance and ransom negotiation dynamics not explained in the summary?
Which African countries, industries, and firm sizes are most affected, and why is the continent treated as a monolith rather than examining specific vulnerability patterns?

articles.title: Tinubu’s Allies Stay With Him, Where Are Opposition Allies? – Fashola
articles.summary: Former Minister of Works, Power and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has questioned the loyalty of political allies of opposition leaders and presidential hopefuls, arguing that President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain both allies and former opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity. Fashola stated this during an exclusive interview with Arise News on Friday, where […]
articles.hausa_translation: Tinubu's Allies Sun Gida Da Shi, Ina Ne Allies Na Opposition? – Fashola. Babatunde Fashola, tsohon Ministan Aiki, Wutar Lantarki Da Gida, ya yi tambaya game da aminci ga 'yan tayi na shugabannin opposition da neman shugaban kasa, yana jada cewa iyawar Shugaban kasa Bola Tinubu na rikonin masu tayi da tsoffin abokan gida yana nuna iyawar sarrafi bambanci a Nigeria.
critical_questions: Who benefits from Fashola's framing that Tinubu's retention of allies demonstrates superior leadership – is this objective analysis or strategic political messaging?
Why does the article not include substantive responses from opposition leaders or allies to Fashola's claims about their loyalty defections?
What specific evidence exists for Fashola's assertion that opposition allies are abandoning their leaders, or is this largely anecdotal?
Is Fashola's comparison of alliance retention between ruling party and opposition parties accounting for structural advantages the ruling party inherently possesses?
What is the timing and incentive for this statement now – is it connected to recent political developments or defections that the article doesn't specify?

articles.title: BREAKING: Bandits Set Homes, Shops Ablaze In Fresh Attack On Niger Community
articles.summary: Armed bandits have reportedly attacked Lumma Sanke in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, setting homes, shops and other properties ablaze and displacing several residents. The attack reportedly occurred on Friday evening, November 27, with local accounts and videos circulating from the area indicating that the attackers targeted Kambari families. Several families, including women […
articles.hausa_translation: SAURI: Balagagi suka kona gida, shagunan da kayan mallaka a sabon kai a gida Lumma Sanke, Borgu, Niger State. Kai kusan jiya, Jiya 27 ga Novemba, an ce balagagi suka kai hari da suka kona mallefi da gida, kuma an ce suka yi wa dangi Kambari. Yawancin iyali sun tafi daga gidansu.
critical_questions: Who are these 'armed bandits' and what is their stated motivation - is this banditry for ransom, territorial conflict, or organized political violence?
Why were Kambari families specifically targeted - does this indicate ethnic targeting, resource competition, or retaliation for prior incidents?
What is the security response status and why does a community have to rely on circulating videos rather than official government incident reports?
What is the displacement scale and humanitarian status of evacuated residents - are there casualty figures, and where are displaced persons seeking refuge?
Is this part of an escalating pattern in Borgu LGA - what are the previous attack frequencies and what do local authorities cite as root causes?

articles.summary: The federal government is looking up to adopt fresh measures to deliver on its promise to offset power sector debts by 2027. In addition to direct payments, Government is considering offsetting outstanding debts against royalties and taxes that electricity producers owe the state. Negotiations are also underway with state-owned oil company NNPC Ltd to lower […]
articles.hausa_translation: Gwamnati ake neman rage kasuwar gas, sabon tsarin biyan jari don kawar da bashi na wuyan wuyan
critical_questions: What specific evidence supports the government's confidence in meeting the 2027 debt offset deadline, and what happens if targets are missed?
How will offsetting debts against royalties and taxes affect transparency, and which stakeholders benefit most from this arrangement?
Why are negotiations with NNPC for lower gas prices not publicly detailed, and what are the terms being offered?
Which electricity producers are most indebted, and will smaller operators be disadvantaged by this repayment model?

articles.title: Ebomhe: Oshoala’s master’s degree will inspire young female footballers

articles.title: CAF introduces VAR for Champions League, Confederation Cup matches

articles.title: [VIDEO] Why Mock Accreditation Won’t Have Logos, Names Of Political Parties — INEC

The exercise will be held across 17,676 selected polling units to test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections.

critical_questions: Why is INEC specifically excluding party logos and names from mock accreditation when parties are key stakeholders whose confidence also matters for election credibility?

Which stakeholder groups (civil society, election observers, opposition parties) were consulted before this decision, and whose voices are missing from this announcement?

critical_questions: What specific evidence does Yiaga Africa present that low turnout would 'undermine' the exercise, versus this being a predictable outcome for a mock accreditation?

What happens to the data collected during this mock accreditation, and who has access to it?
Are election observers, civil society organizations, and opposition parties given equal access to monitor and verify this testing process?

articles.title: Nigeria’s $1bn Monthly Remittance Has Been Achieved – CBN Governor Cardoso

The Central Bank of Nigeria says the country now targets $1.5 billion in monthly remittances by the end of the first half of 2027.

articles.hausa_translation: Jigon remittances na Nigeria na dala miliyan 1 an gani - Govnon CBN Cardoso. Banki Tsakiya na Nijeriya ya ce kasuwar remittances ya kaiwa dala miliyan 1 a waje jiya, amma sai an kara buri ga dala miliyan 1.5 a wannan shekara 2027.

Is CBN's optimism about remittances masking underlying currency instability or capital flight concerns that might require remittances to prop up forex reserves?

articles.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
articles.summary:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked […]
The post Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Be
articles.hausa_translation: An jari kawar wajen kashe jami'in NSCDC a Benue. Shugaban Agatu Local Government Area, Melvin Ejeh, ya yi alqali na kama da dakatar da waɗanda suka kashe jami'in NSCDC, Inspector Anyebe Anya. An ce 'yan bindiga suka kasar shi. Jama'a suna neman sakamakon gida.
critical_questions: What specific details are missing about the attack—when, where, how many attackers, and what weapons were used?

What concrete steps beyond a 'vow' has the LG chairman taken, and why is there no statement from NSCDC headquarters?
Is this incident part of a pattern of violence in Agatu, and are there political or economic interests at stake in the response?
